intro: Accra rewards visitors with lively markets, Atlantic beaches, and a deep cultural pulse. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; TroTros (minibuses) are the main public transport.
TroTros run fixed routes; a 'mate' calls out destinations.
Taxis rarely use meters; agree the fare before you ride.
Ride apps that work: Uber, Bolt, Yango, InDrive.
Hiring a car with driver is common for sightseeing.
Walking is fine by day; watch for open drains and traffic.

nkrumah.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
nkrumah.price_text: ≈ GHS 20–40 for non-Ghanaians; check on the day
nkrumah.tip: The mausoleum and small museum tell Ghana's independence story; go early to beat the heat.

independence.name: Independence Square
independence.tip: The Black Star Gate and arches face the sea; bring water, there is little shade.

osu-castle.name: Osu Castle
osu-castle.price_text: Exterior free; interior access is restricted — check on the day
osu-castle.hours: Not reliably open to the public
osu-castle.tip: It is a government building, so view it from outside and ask locally before planning a visit.

makola.name: Makola Market
makola.price_text: Free to enter; bring small cash for purchases
makola.tip: Go with a local guide, keep bags in front and expect to bargain.

jamestown.name: Jamestown Lighthouse
jamestown.price_text: Small entry fee, roughly GHS 5–20 — check on the day
jamestown.tip: Walk the old harbour lanes below the lighthouse for the best photos.

jollof.name: Jollof Rice (Ghana)
jollof.price_text: ≈ GHS 30–80 a plate at a sit-down spot
jollof.tip: Try it with grilled chicken or fried fish; ask for shito on the side.

labadi-beach.name: Labadi Beach
labadi-beach.price_text: ≈ GHS 10–30 entry — check on the day
labadi-beach.tip: Weekends bring music and food stalls; keep valuables close and swim with care.

artists-alliance.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
artists-alliance.hours: Roughly Mon–Sat 09:00–18:00 — check on the day
artists-alliance.tip: Three floors of Ghanaian art near the beach; good for gifts.

osu-walk.name: Osu Oxford Street walk
osu-walk.tip: The main strip for shops, cafes and nightlife; walk it in the evening when it cools.

accra-tour.name: Accra city walking tour
accra-tour.tip: A guide helps with markets and history; agree the price and stops before you start.

duke.name: Duke of York restaurant
duke.tip: Reliable spot for Ghanaian and international dishes in Osu.

kempinski-view.name: Kempinski Gold Coast rooftop view
kempinski-view.tip: Go up for a drink at sunset for city and sea views.

accra-mall.name: Accra Mall
accra-mall.tip: Air-conditioned shops and food court; handy on a hot or rainy afternoon.

wli-note.name: Day trip to Aburi Botanical Gardens
wli-note.tip: Cooler hills north of Accra; arrange a car and driver for the day.

labone-cafe.name: Labone coffee and brunch strip
labone-cafe.price_text: ≈ GHS 60–140 for coffee and a plate
labone-cafe.tip: Quiet leafy streets with cafes; good for a slow morning.

cantonments-walk.name: Cantonments embassy district walk
cantonments-walk.tip: Green, calm streets; combine with a nearby cafe stop.

national-museum.name: National Museum of Ghana
national-museum.hours: Roughly Tue–Sun daytime — verify before going
national-museum.tip: Collections on Ghanaian history and culture; call ahead as hours can change.

kejetia-note.name: Osu Night Market food stalls
kejetia-note.tip: Street food like kelewele and grilled fish; eat where locals queue.

black-star-square-note.name: Black Star Square sunset walk
black-star-square-note.tip: Pair with Independence Square for sea breezes at dusk.

airport-cafe.name: Airport Residential cafe and shop stop
airport-cafe.tip: Modern cafes near the airport; useful before a flight.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Jamestown, Makola Market and live highlife.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Jollof, waakye and chop bars across the city.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Labadi and Bojo Beach plus a coastal drive.

stays.why: Walk to restaurants, bars and Oxford Street shops. Central for nightlife and easy taxi rides to the old town.
Closest to the airport and big hotels. Quiet streets, good for early flights and business trips.
Leafy and calm, with cafés and embassies nearby. A short ride from Osu and the beaches.
Quiet, upscale and central. Good for longer stays and travellers who want space and security.

food: Try Ghanaian staples: jollof rice, waakye (rice and beans), banku with tilapia, and fufu with light soup.
Chop bars are cheap local canteens. Expect a filling plate for roughly GHS 30–60; check the price first.
For red-red (beans, plantain and palm oil) and grilled tilapia, look around Osu and Labadi.
Street snacks: kelewele (spiced fried plantain), kebab skewers and roasted corn. Eat where it is busy and freshly cooked.
Book ahead for popular weekend spots. Many kitchens close early on Sundays; check on the day.
more_time: Add a day for Cape Coast and Elmina castles, about 2–3 hours west by road. Go early and hire a driver.
Swap one city day for Aburi Botanical Gardens and the hills, roughly an hour north of Accra.
Beach lovers can trade a city afternoon for Bojo Beach or a boat trip on the Volta near Ada.
